Done. Reflection summary:

What went wrong: My USD-side extraction was **perfect** — the Nov-minus-Dec 1959 total trust-account receipts difference was 530.0 M USD (gold back-solves to exactly that). The entire error was the exchange rate. The question asked for the *monthly* average USD-CAD rate for December 1959, but I used the *annual* 1959 average (0.9590 CAD/USD), producing 508.27. Gold (504.12) requires the December monthly rate ≈ 0.9512 — about 0.8% lower, because CAD strengthened through late 1959 so month-end months ran below the annual mean.

Why this was generalizable (and worth saving): The failure was caused by a **wrong instruction in my own existing skill**. The `currency-and-geomean.md` reference literally said monthly pre-1971 CAD data "is NOT online... use the Officer annual figure" — and even contained the exact wrong worked example "530 USD * 0.9590 = 508.27 CAD." That guidance directly produced this graded-wrong answer.

What I changed:
- Rewrote that section of `references/currency-and-geomean.md` to flag that "MONTHLY average rate" must use the month-specific value, that the annual figure is a last-resort fallback only, where the monthly pre-1971 USD-CAD rate actually lives (Federal Reserve Bulletin FX table on FRASER, Jan/Feb 1960 issue for Dec 1959), and the diagnostic signature (final off <1% with solid USD side → suspect annual-where-monthly).
- Updated memory with the compact version of the same lesson, including the back-solved Dec 1959 ≈ 0.9512 figure.

This was a genuine self-correction of stale skill guidance, not per-question trivia.
